annotations.note: FY25 Adj EBITDA $4.98bn, net debt $742m (0.14x); H126 EBITDA $3.41bn, gross debt $7.10bn, net debt $2.05bn.
100% of crude/refined product export proceeds flow directly into offshore collection accounts; debt service for international Eurobonds is deducted prior to any fiscal repatriation.
Low cash lifting cost ($8 - $18/boe) ensures robust operating profitability and positive cash flow even during severe oil price downturns ($50/bbl).
Proved plus probable commercial reserves provide a durable 12-18 year production life, underpinning long-dated senior paper.

verdict.summary: S&P upgraded KMG to BBB Stable (SACP to bbb-) on 02-Sep-26 alongside Kazakhstan's sovereign upgrade. 1H26 revenue hit KZT 5,568bn with EBITDA KZT 1,655bn (+45% YoY) and FCF KZT 765bn, backed by Tengizchevroil JV dividends. Proactively tendered $500m of 2030 USD notes and priced CNY 3.5bn Dim Sum bonds at 2.3%-2.8% coupons. Key risks: CPC export disruptions and Samruk-Kazyna bond holdings.

positives: Rating uplift: Upgraded by S&P to BBB Stable (SACP bbb-) in Sep-26; Moody's Baa1 Stable, Fitch BBB Stable.
Strong 1H26 cash generation: Revenue KZT 5,568bn, EBITDA KZT 1,655bn (+45% YoY), FCF KZT 765bn supported by KZT 500bn TCO dividends.
Proactive liability management: Tendered $500m of $1.25bn 5.375% 2030 notes and issued CNY 3.5bn (~$490m) 5Y/10Y Dim Sum bonds at 2.3%-2.8%.
negatives: Export & output vulnerability: CPC pipeline disruption cut July output 14% MoM and trimmed 2026 target to 96mt (from 98mt).
Related-party liquidity question: Net debt rose to KZT 983bn as cash was deployed into parent Samruk-Kazyna coupon bonds.
Legacy repo 2021A-2024A USD table is unverified and needs filing rebuild.
